Assassination Rogue Rotation in
The rotation for Assassination Rogue focuses on a simple build/spend rotation, but instead of optimizing around short cooldowns or swapping between buttons, Assassination is a slow spec, with purposeful downtime that rewards playing around the gaps in your rotation correctly.
Preparing for AOE:
Our AoE is enabled through
Caustic Spatter
and
Crimson Tempest
. Crimson tempest especially is a very expensive button in terms of energy, and knowing when AoE is going to happen in an encounter will allow you to plan around it with your cooldowns, bleeds, and resources.
Managing Envenom Uptime:
Implacable
enables a pooling playstyle that will require players to drop the buff from
Envenom
at regular intervals in order to get energy back. Managing this without overcapping resources will be the key to success.
Energy Efficiency:
Assassination is not locked by the GCD, and is instead locked by Energy. Because of this, you will want to think about what button is most efficient at a given time, rather than forcing yourself to cast something every time its possible.

Assassination Rogue Major Cooldowns
Assassination has access to a variety of different cooldowns on its spec tree. All of them come with some extra wrinkles in how they work rather than simply being flat increases, so the below section covers
how
they work, and most importantly, how to get the most out of each use.
Deathmark
Deathmark
is a single target debuff with a 2 minute cooldown. Aim to be casting it on cooldown, and aligning all other cooldowns to it, as its interactions will dictate your burst. Deathmark has a number of effects:
Applies a Bleed
Restores Energy
Doubles the Damage of
Garrote
,
Rupture
, and Lethal Poisons such as
Deadly Poison
and
Amplifying Poison
When a Lethal Poison is applied to the target, it is instead applied twice
The last two points are the most important to our burst. Doubling the damage of Garrote includes the empowered
Improved Garrote
from stealth for example. Applying a Lethal Poison twice interacts with the ramping nature of
Kingsbane
, causing it to do significantly more damage.
Some other talents interact with Deathmark in passive ways, such as
Finish the Job
, and
Lethal Dose
. This makes it both worth to cast Deathmark for AoE, and further empowers it as a single target cooldown.
Kingsbane
Kingsbane
is a single target debuff with a 1 minute cooldown. Aim to be casting it on cooldown, and aligning it to
Deathmark
, as it will ramp faster during the window. Kingsbane is a two-part attack:
An Instant hit of damage, generating a combo point
A 14 second damage over time effect which increases with every poison application during the effect
Deathmark is a strong boost to Kingsbane, as the duplicated poison applications greatly speed up the ramp time on Kingsbane's DoT effect.
Vanish
Vanish
is a two minute cooldown that enables the usage of
Improved Garrote
. This is the only remaining interaction with Stealth in Midnight for Assassination Rogues, and as such, Vanish is essentially just an enabler of Improved Garrote. In single target this should be treated as an extension of
Deathmark
, where as in mythic+, it should be seen as a way to get a restealth.
Improved Garrote can be used in multiple situations, but there are two key ways to leverage it that should be noted in Single target and AoE rotations.
Deathmark
increases the damage of
Garrote
by 100%, so having Improved Garrote for this window is ideal to boost burst and single target damage.
Crimson Tempest
spreads Improved Garrote to multiple targets without having to manually cast Garrotes on each target
Assassination Rogue Advanced Tips
The biggest optimizations for Assassination Rogue are regarding energy efficiency, as this is the major limiting resource for the spec.
Pooling and Implacable
Pooling is something often stated as a core feature of Assassination, and while it's true that pooling can have an impact (around 1.5% currently), the only way this materializes in the rotation is playing around the buff from
Implacable
.
Implacable, our new Apex Talent, is a stacking buff that grants a burst of energy regeneration when the buff from
Envenom
times out from your character, granting increasing amounts of energy depending on how many envenoms were cast before it dropped. This bonus has a maximum of 80% and ramps with each envenom cast:
20%
35%
50%
65%
80%
The Implacable buff on your character will show the current percentage as a stack counter.
To properly play around this, you will want to force yourself to let Envenom expire when hitting 80%, so long as you will not be overcapping energy in the process. After all, getting a burst of energy is only good if you actually can use it! This is most relevant for Single Target, but can also have uses in lower target AoE.
Darkest Night and Shiv
Shiv
might not give any debuff anymore and not be used rotationally, but it lives on for builds due to some awkward tuning lining up for a perfect storm.
Even with it not being required anymore, the buff from
Darkest Night
is so large that we will continue to cast
Envenom
with maximum combo points if the buff is up. The addition of
Toxic Stiletto
on the talent tree then opens up another layer to this. Because it reduces the energy cost of Shiv so heavily, it becomes worth it to cast Shiv if you're 1 away from maximum combo points. Casting a regular generator such as
Mutilate
would be much more expensive and waste combo points in the process, where as Shiv ends up being a cheap option to get that last combo point.
